method: per-new-VO adequacy for the 11 freeze-v4 VOs: sensors + corpus sweep, facets, composability, contradiction duty

candidate_tests.facets: POSITIVE (strong): two generic instantiations calc::add::<i32> (count 2) + calc::add::<u64> (regions max 3) aggregate to Some(5) — proves per-target summation and generic aggregation. NEGATIVE-REJECTION (strong): other::add in src/other.rs, count 99, matches the name but fails the filename condition and contributes none while co-present functions do contribute. Also: absent item-path 'subtract' -> None. UNPROVEN: name-condition rejection while others still contribute (only wholesale absence is shown); mangled symbols never flow through this function (names are pre-demangled literals), so demangling is not composed here; no probe of suffix boundaries.

POSITIVE: _RNvCs..12calc_fixture3add demangles and matches item-path 'add' — proves the demangle step of one match condition. NEGATIVE-REJECTION: ..8evaluate vs 'add' is false. But this is a plain non-match, not a suffix-boundary probe: no case where the demangled name ends with the item-path as a raw substring but not at a '::' segment boundary (e.g. calc::readd), which is where the claim's literal 'ends with' and runner.rs:309 diverge. UNPROVEN: summation, filename condition, aggregation, generic-instantiation naming — the test exercises llvm_name_matches in isolation, never llvm_cov_function_count.

POSITIVE (weak): a single function matching both conditions with count 0 yields Some(0), showing a matched-but-zero function is summed (0) rather than treated as unmatched — supports 'sum over every matching function' at the degenerate cardinality. Currently covers VO-ARUST-003 and is remapped to VO-EXEC-07, not VO-EXEC-15. NEGATIVE-REJECTION: none. BOUNDARY: none; one function, no aggregation, no rejection arm.

POSITIVE (weak, but the only end-to-end): real cargo-llvm-cov run; evidence.target_execution.count >= 1 for the declared target src/lib.rs::known — proves a declared target's measured count reaches Evidence through the attribution path with real llvm-cov JSON (not a hand-written fixture). Asserts only >=1, so no aggregation, no match-condition discrimination, single target. NEGATIVE-REJECTION: none. BOUNDARY: none.

Exercises the uncalled-target path (count 0 -> target_execution FAIL). That is the count->verdict mapping of §10.2, not this claim's attribution/summation rule. No matching-set discrimination and no aggregation; relevant surface, no facet of the claim.

details.contradiction_evidence: No contradiction. runner.rs:266-305 sums every function passing both gates and skips the rest (`if !llvm_name_matches(..) || !llvm_filenames_match(..) { continue; }`, :279-283; `total = total.saturating_add(function_count)`, :301; `matched.then_some(total)`, :304) — matching 詳細設計 §10.2 ("demangle 済み関数名の末尾が locator の item-path と一致し、かつ filenames のいずれかの末尾が locator の path と一致 … 同じtargetに対応するcountを合算する"). Three residuals stay inside spec ambiguity, not against it: llvm_name_matches (:307-322) requires a `::` boundary or `item_path::<…>`, stricter than a literal "ends with"; path_suffix_matches (:337-341) is a raw suffix, looser; and a matched function with neither `count` nor `regions` aborts the whole sum via `?` (:299).
details.notes: Sensors compose over one surface: 006 tests llvm_name_matches, which 004's llvm_cov_function_count calls (:279) — same module, same call chain. Together they prove positive aggregation of generic instantiations, filename-condition rejection amid contributors, and demangling in isolation. Not PROVEN because: (1) no test drives a mangled symbol through llvm_cov_function_count, so "demangled name" is never composed with "sum"; (2) name-condition rejection is only shown as wholesale absence (None), never as one function contributing none while siblings contribute; (3) both suffix boundaries (`::` segment, path separator) and the missing-count/regions abort are unprobed. Recommend at remap: keep both sensors on VO-EXEC-15 and add a mangled-symbol-in-report case plus a suffix-boundary negative.

candidate_tests.facets: Positive facet at the named surface: same fixture, byte_range.start/end +100, assert_eq! on hash_test_subject (vtest-model/src/lib.rs:1123-1153). All fields the claim enumerates are held identical (fixture_location/fixture_execution clones), so the field-identity precondition is exactly instantiated. Gaps: SourceRange also carries start_line/end_line (lib.rs:295-301) and both stay 1/1 — the realistic relocation delta (line numbers move) is never varied; a single +100 instance, no zero-length/adjacent/overlapping ranges; equality alone is vacuity-exposed (a constant hash would pass) with no in-test discrimination assertion. No negative-rejection facet exists for an invariance claim.

Non-degeneracy guard, same module and same synthetic_test_hash fixture (lib.rs:1111-1119): changing intent yields assert_ne!, so the subject hash is not constant and TEST-MODEL-005's equality is not vacuous. Composes over the identical contract surface. Does not vary byte range at all, and shows sensitivity for only 1 of the ~14 hashed slots, so it bounds vacuity only weakly.

Calls hash_test_subject (vtest-adapter-api/tests/w1_acceptance_binding.rs:296) but asserts only that the DTO is hash-free and hash != ContentHash::from_text(construct). No byte-range-only pair; byte_range appears solely as fixture data. Relevance without proof.

Exercises the production hashing call site materialize_discovery_batch → hash_test_subject (vtest-scan/src/lib.rs:235-248) with a real SourceRange, but pins only construct and target hashes and asserts managed hash != construct hash (lib.rs:1523-1571). No two subjects differing only in byte range, so the pipeline surface carries no evidence for the exclusion.

Also an exclusion-from-subject claim (SRC ID does not move the hash, vtest-scan/src/lib.rs:1611-1633), but on the Source Target subject and a different excluded input. Different subject domain; does not compose onto the Test subject byte-range claim.

details.contradiction_evidence: No contradiction. hash_test_subject (crates/vtest-model/src/lib.rs:394-455) enumerates the subject fields explicitly and includes only "location.adapter" (:424), "location.path" (:428), "location.locator" (:432) — no byte_range/SourceRange entry anywhere in the field list; SourceRange (:304-308) is reachable only via SourceLocation.byte_range (:315), which is never read there. The production path passes the same location struct through unchanged (crates/vtest-scan/src/lib.rs:235-248), so the omission holds end-to-end. Implementation matches SPEC-BASIC §1 line 31 and SPEC-ACCEPT §18.3.9 line 203 ("byte range自体は含めず").
details.notes: Corpus sweep: grep of byte_range/hash_test_subject over all crates and tests finds no other test holding every other field fixed while varying the range; remaining hits are fixtures, CLI display (cli/src/lib.rs:1594-1623), or range-driven byte extraction. Evidence composes (MODEL-004 + MODEL-005 share one fixture and one surface) but does not close the positive facet: the line-number component of SourceRange is never moved, and no scan-level or downstream-consumer (approval staleness after relocation) instance exists. Suggested closing test: shift start_line/end_line only, plus a materialize_discovery_batch pair relocated in-file.

candidate_tests.facets: POSITIVE: init's on-disk .verify/config.yaml contains `version: 2`, `adapters:`, `id: rust-cargo` (adapter_acceptance.rs:823-839) - proves v2-ness and the built-in entry's presence. NOT covered: the assertions are unanchored substring checks, so roots / scan / scan.assertion_macros / run being nested UNDER the adapter entry is unevidenced here; no absence check for a top-level flat scan:/run: block. NEGATIVE-REJECTION: none. BOUNDARY: only the default init path (one project name, one built-in adapter); no other command's writes are enumerated.

POSITIVE (strongest): to_yaml of a v2 config emits `assertion_macros:` with 8-space item indent (store/lib.rs:641), i.e. under adapters[].scan; `parsed == expected` full-struct equality after from_yaml forces version==2, roots, scan.include, assertion_macros, run.coverage to survive - and from_yaml rejects top-level scan/run at v2 (lib.rs:265-269) and empty roots, so equality is only reachable if the emission is adapter-namespaced. NOT covered: the negative universal (writer never emits flat v1), and init's file itself. BOUNDARY: single rust-cargo adapter only.

POSITIVE (weak): default_for -> to_yaml -> from_yaml preserves project.name, rust_cargo().scan.include, run.coverage (lib.rs:605-611). Alone it cannot distinguish v1 from v2 output: the v1 reader synthesises a rust-cargo AdapterSection (lib.rs:258-263), so rust_cargo() would succeed even on flat v1 emission. It asserts no version field and no YAML shape. NEGATIVE/BOUNDARY: none.

ADJACENT NEGATIVE: byte-compares .verify/config.yaml before/after `vtest verify` on a v1 project (adapter_acceptance.rs:583-597) - proves verify emits no config at all, hence no flat v1 emission on that path. Does not touch the writer's output shape, init, or any other command.

ADJACENT NEGATIVE: hand-written flat v1 config (no full_scope) survives `verify` byte-identical (adapter_acceptance.rs:604-620+). Same narrow support for 'v1 never emitted' restricted to the verify surface; no writer-surface or init evidence.
Writes a v2 `adapters: []` config by hand and asserts scan fails closed (E-ADAPTER-001). Exercises the reader/registry, not anything the system writes. No facet of this claim.

Unmapped (no @vtest.id). Asserts a checked-in FIXTURE file config/v2-rust-cargo.yaml contains `version: 2` / `id: rust-cargo` (line 393-396). Fixture bytes are authored, never system-written, so it evidences nothing about the writer or init.

details.contradiction_evidence:
Not fired. ProjectConfig::to_yaml still carries a live flat version-1 branch (store/lib.rs:195-212): `if self.version == 1 { ... out.push_str("scan:
  include:
"); ... out.push_str("run:
  coverage: ...") ; return out; }`. A version-1 ProjectConfig can exist (from_yaml compat read, lib.rs:252-263), so the writer is capable of emitting the flat layout. But the only production write of config.yaml is init_project (lib.rs:502-503) using default_for -> version 2, and the only other ProjectConfig constructor is from_yaml (lib.rs:554, read-only). No reachable caller writes a v1 config back, so this is a local latent branch, not a system-level contradiction (same calibration as VO-EXEC-14).
details.notes: Claim is faithful to the spec: 基本仕様 §2.4 L116 and 別紙C §18.3.9 L211 state the writer and `vtest init` emit the version-2 adapter namespace. Composition is genuine - init_project calls default_for().to_yaml(), the exact function TEST-STORE-010/012 exercise - so the positive facets (v2 document, adapters namespace, rust-cargo entry, roots/scan/assertion_macros/run nested under the entry) hold over one contract surface. PROVEN blocked by two gaps: (1) the universal negative "flat v1 is never emitted" has no test - to_yaml's v1 branch is never pinned unreachable, only grep-confirmed; (2) "every config.yaml the system writes" is evidenced only for init and (via TEST-CLI-014/015) verify's non-writing; other commands are unenumerated.

candidate_tests.facets: Positive: direct byte compare of the three leaf encodings (crates/vtest-model/src/lib.rs:1191-1198) proves Null/String("")/List([]) are pairwise distinct. Not covered: no ContentHash is ever computed, so the subject-level claim ("never share a content hash") is only inferred from framing; no field-position or nested case (null vs "" vs [] inside a Map/List field); no other subject builder exercised (hash_test_subject Option fields, hash_execution_state_subject.head_revision, hash_record_subject); no empty-Map vs Null case. Negative-rejection facet is a universal negative spot-checked at three values. No boundary case (e.g. List([String("")]) vs List([])).

Compositional bridge only: shows a CanonicalProjection reaches a real subject hash via encode() and that a changed projection changes the subject (lib.rs:1163-1184). It varies a string value, never null/empty/empty-list, so it supplies the leaf-to-subject link the claim needs but proves no facet of the null/empty distinction itself.
Domain separation and cross-type reuse (lib.rs:1205-1215). Same encoder surface, different property; contributes nothing to null/empty/empty-list distinctness.

Preserves absent (None) vs empty ([]) dependency closure across YAML round-trip (records.rs:2468-2507). No content hash is computed, and None never reaches hash_approval_subject — it is rejected earlier as ClosureAbsent (approval.rs:211-213). Adjacent surface, not the hash contract.

details.contradiction_evidence: None — implementation is faithful. crates/vtest-model/src/lib.rs:180 `Self::Null => output.extend_from_slice(b"null")`; :194 String goes through `encode_projection_value(output, b"string", ...)` (8-byte tag len + tag + 8-byte value len); :195-197 `List` emits b"list" + 8-byte count. So Null=4B, String("")=22B, List([])=12B — pairwise distinct preimages. SubjectEncoder::field (:144-149) length-prefixes name and value, keeping per-field substitution injective; hash_test_subject/hash_execution_state_subject route Option fields through canonical_json (:429-431, :916) yielding Null, and vtest-store/src/approval.rs:409-410 `optional_text` = `value.map_or(CanonicalProjection::Null, text)`. Spec 詳細設計 §1.3 L79 states the same rule.
details.notes: Corpus sweep (grep for CanonicalProjection::Null/empty constructors, assert_ne over hashes, hash-related @vtest.intent) found no test beyond the four above; all `ContentHash::from_subject` call sites live in vtest-model, so the contract surface is closed and auditable. Gap to PROVEN: no test composes leaf distinctness into an actual subject hash pair, and none covers nested or per-builder positions. Precision note for remap: the guarantee is encoding-level. Upstream carriers can collapse the distinction before a subject exists (VoRecord.combinations is `Vec` with serde default, so YAML `null` and `[]` both yield []); that is not a collision under the claim, but the claim should not be read as protecting the YAML surface.

Boundary-ambiguity: pins the numeric value 2 but never applies it as the <=2 filter. Consistent with the prior calibration (dogfood-shadow-mapping.json:680 gave it NO for the same reason).

crates/vtest-cli/tests/m9_acceptance.rs:1222-1263. MCP tools/call failure envelope: isError, ok=false, E-OP-001, structuredContent diagnostics[0].candidates[0] == src/lib.rs::known. Positive: extends envelope surfacing to the MCP transport. Negative-rejection and boundary: same limits as TEST-CLI-085 — single-symbol fixture, only candidates[0] asserted, no exclusion case, no ordering, no distance-boundary discrimination.

crates/vtest-cli/tests/m9_acceptance.rs:1265-1401. Fail-closed error matrix; the invalid-symbol row asserts diagnostics[0].candidates[0] == src/lib.rs::known. Positive: candidate emission survives a mixed protocol/usage-error sequence without audit writes. Negative-rejection: covers other rejection codes, not candidate-set membership. Boundary: identical single-assertion limitation; contributes envelope durability, not the ordering or tail-segment rule.

details.contradiction_evidence: No contradiction. Current implementation matches the claim: crates/vtest-adapter-rust/src/operations_support.rs:294-329 — symbol_candidates takes the requested tail via rsplit_once("::"), builds exact_suffix from indexed sources whose locator.item_path tail `candidate == item`, then near from tails with `edit_distance(candidate, item) <= 2`, dedupes exacts out of near (line 326) and appends near after exact (line 327). Reached from the E-OP-001 failure paths at operations_support.rs:122/132 and crates/vtest-scan/src/operations.rs:458/469/847/859, all via Diagnostic::with_candidates (crates/vtest-model/src/lib.rs:708) rendered into the common envelope.
details.notes: Two gaps block PROVEN. (1) The distinctive composite — exact-tail matches FOLLOWED BY near matches — is exercised nowhere: no fixture holds both a same-tail item and a near-miss item, so cross-bucket ordering is unobservable in the corpus. Every candidate test has either an empty exact bucket (TEST-CLI-004) or a single-symbol index (TEST-CLI-085/096/097). (2) No test discriminates tail-segment matching from whole-locator matching: "knwon"→"known" is distance 2 either way, "ad"→"add" distance 1 either way. Also untested: the <=2 edge (distance 2 accepted vs 3 rejected) at the filter level. Evidence composes for near-bucket inclusion, coarse exclusion, and envelope surfacing across CLI and MCP — hence PARTIAL, not UNSUPPORTED.

details.contradiction_evidence: No contradiction. Implementation read: crates/vtest-model/src/lib.rs:113-129 — "let normalized_endings = text.replace(\"\\r\\n\", \"\\n\").replace('\\r', \"\\n\");" then per split_inclusive('\n') line "normalized.push_str(body.trim_end_matches([' ', '\\t']));" re-appending '\n' only when present. details.notes: PARTIAL: the closure leg composes on one surface; the positive leg is a single conflated assertion and the "only after normalization" quantifier is never exercised on a subject hash. Two divergences, both below the contradiction bar. (1) Claim precision: lib.rs:123 trims only space and tab, so a line ending in VT/FF/U+3000 keeps it and the hash changes — under a literal "trailing whitespace" the impl under-normalizes. (2) crates/vtest-scan/src/lib.rs:167 hashes construct bytes via ContentHash::from_bytes, unnormalized, into DiscoveredTest.content_hash — but that field has no consumer outside vtest-scan, so it is unobservable, not a defect.

details.contradiction_evidence: No contradiction. ContentHash::from_subject (crates/vtest-model/src/lib.rs:74-83) delegates to SubjectEncoder, whose new() emits the domain as the first named field and whose field() writes u64-BE len(name) + name + u64-BE len(value) + value (lib.rs:131-155) — domain separator plus named length-prefixed fields, never plain concatenation. All from_subject callsites are in vtest-model with 8 pairwise-distinct domain literals (lib.rs:422, 469, 484, 500, 511, 577, 587, 909). Length-prefix framing makes the encoding injective, so distinct domains structurally cannot collide. Implementation is faithful to the claim.
details.notes: Universal quantifiers ("each", "never", "pairwise") rest on code inspection; tests reach 2/28 domain pairs and concat-rejection for 2/8 kinds. Unproven: framing boundary (("ab","c") vs ("a","bc")), domain-field length prefix, 6 kinds' concat rejection. Two scope notes for remap: (1) VO and REQ share vtest:record-subject:v1 (approval.rs:116,133; design §1.3 L86 sanctions it) — read as distinct kinds, "pairwise distinct" fails there; key-set differences make collision impractical, not separated. Recommend precising "subject kind" = the 8 §1.3 domains, as done for VO-ADAPTER-15. (2) Source hashes (hash_specification_source, construct from_bytes) carry no domain — outside the claim's subject scope.

details.contradiction_evidence: Violating surface = core find_target_source, the self-declared "one resolution path (§6.1, §907)", crates/vtest-scan/src/lib.rs:67-80: `TargetRef::Locator { .. } => scan.sources.iter().find(|source| source.target == *target)`. `.find()` returns the FIRST of N duplicates, so a 2+ match resolves instead of staying unresolved. cross_entity_diagnostics (same file, ~1320-1332) does count correctly — `locators.get(...).copied() == Some(1)` — but only EMITS E-SCAN-004; resolution proceeds. Consumers apply no arity guard: vtest-verify/src/lib.rs:869-880 `declared_canonical_targets` treats Some(source) as resolved; vtest-audit/src/lib.rs:241 persists `source.target.normalized()` as the audit subject. TEST-SCAN-011's cfg-duplicate fixture proves the 2-entry index state is constructible. This is cluster 4 (target-resolution-ambiguity-collapsed, CONFIRMED) reaching this VO.
details.notes: Linkage verified concretely, not assumed: the diagnostic surface honors the claim, the resolution surface does not — that split is the defect. Secondary contradiction (adapter side, static_audit.rs:1361-1405): resolve_target/find_function honors 0/2+ arity but resolves on a unique SUFFIX match, i.e. not "matches it exactly", and is an independent per-subsystem candidate scan over a re-parse, which 詳細設計 §907 forbids ("各subsystemが独自にcandidate列を走査して1件を選ぶ経路を持ってはならない"). details.contradiction_evidence: Step 3 does not fire. The delegation locus is single and hardcoded: vtest-cli/src/lib.rs:348 `let discovery = registry.source_discovery(&AdapterId::new(RUST_CARGO_ADAPTER_ID))?;` and vtest-scan/src/lib.rs:400 `scan_project_with_discovery(root, config, &RustCargoDiscovery)`; `scan_project_with_discovery` (:408-416) takes one `&dyn SourceDiscoveryAdapter`. No production caller of `ids()` exists. But vtest-store/src/lib.rs:375 rejects every id but `rust-cargo` ("unknown adapter"), and built_in_registry (cli:339) registers exactly one. So every reachable run has registered set {rust-cargo} and sequence [rust-cargo], vacuously satisfying both clauses — no product-surface counterexample can be built. The mismatch is intensional (mechanism shape), not observable divergence.
details.notes: The v4 amendment over-generalized its sensor. TEST-AAPI-002 evidences the registry-enumeration contract (adapter plan v0.2 line 182, "ID順の決定論的な列挙"), already owned by VO-AAPI-002; ADAPTER-17 adds a visiting/delegation clause with zero evidence and zero implementation locus. SPEC-ACCEPT §18.3.9 does assign vtest-scan "adapter discoveryの委譲" and all-adapter merge, but states no ordering rule — so the ordering claim is ontology over-reach, and multi-adapter delegation itself is spec-ahead-of-impl (plan line 658 defers other languages to later milestones). Remap recommendation: either narrow the claim to registry enumeration (then it duplicates VO-AAPI-002) or defer it to the multi-language milestone.

candidate_tests.facets: Positive only, and only the unit constant: parse_form_schema(RUST_UNIT_FUNCTION_FORM) -> kind==rust-unit-function, fields.len()==8, template contains "@vtest.target {target}" (forms.rs:499-505). No per-field type/required/validator assertion, no adapter/ownership, no rust-integration, no registry resolution under a missing Form file, no multi-target ordering. Negative-rejection and boundary facets absent.

Positive, both kinds end-to-end (vtest-cli/src/lib.rs:4207-4497): unit create from answers omitting `file` succeeds; rust-integration create yields targets.len()==2 and kind integration-normal, second target queryable - implying two @vtest.target lines emitted. But root() runs init, which writes both Form files (store/lib.rs:504-511), so the no-user-file premise is untested; declaration order and schema fields unasserted.

Positive, true no-Form-file premise: from_m1_base fixture has no .verify/forms (tests/fixtures/calc/m1/base/.verify), so form_get resolves the built-in constant; asserts data.kind==rust-unit-function and fields is an array (m9_acceptance.rs:570-577). Unit kind only; no field types/required/validators, no integration Form, no exactly-two cardinality.

Negative-rejection facet: form_get kind "unknown-form" on a forms-less project fails E-OP-001 "invalid form" (m9_acceptance.rs:1330-1333, 1394) - no implicit Rust fallback for a third kind. Does not assert that both built-ins resolve, so it bounds the set from above only.

Ownership facet: init writes .verify/forms/{rust-unit-function,rust-integration}.yaml and each contains "adapter: rust-cargo" (adapter_acceptance.rs:823-840). Files-present path, not registry resolution; asserts no schema content, no field/validator/template detail.
Parser strictness (unknown field property rejected on a mutated unit constant, forms.rs:527-534). Exercises parse_form_schema rejection, not the built-in kind set, integration schema, or emission.
Answers-file parsing (inline/block lists). Different contract surface from Form registry resolution and built-in schema declaration.
Asserts the opposite premise: a user-written rust-unit-function.yaml wins and reloads on mtime change (m9_acceptance.rs:427-452). Evidence about user-file precedence, not built-in resolution.

details.contradiction_evidence: The two built-in schemas differ beyond the targets field. crates/vtest-store/src/forms.rs:42-46 (unit) `- name: file` ... `required: false`; forms.rs:98-102 (integration) `- name: file` ... `required: true`. The flag is enforced: vtest-scan/src/operations.rs:920-927 `if field.required && value.is_none_or(FormValue::is_empty)` -> E-OP-001 "required answer `file` is missing". Behavioral asymmetry: unit create omitting `file` succeeds (destination derived from `target`, adapter-rust/operations_support.rs:148-160), integration create omitting `file` is rejected. SPEC-IFACE §14.3 likewise says "他は同一", so spec and impl are desynced on the same point.
details.notes: Secondary "only" breaches (likely intended, cite at remap): template line `@vtest.kind unit-{test_kind}` vs `integration-{test_kind}` (forms.rs:52, 108; operations.rs:340-347), plus title/kind. Gaps regardless of the contradiction: RUST_INTEGRATION_FORM is parsed by no test directly and its missing-file fallback (forms.rs:127-131) is never exercised; one-@vtest.target-line-per-element in declaration order (adapter-rust/operations_support.rs:383-397) is never asserted; §14.3's empty-list/duplicate-target rejection untested. "rust-cargo-owned" is declaration-only: StructuredTestAdapter::built_in_form_kinds (adapter-api/src/lib.rs:438-441) has no implementor and load_form_schema hardcodes the two kinds in core - a nuance, not the contradiction.

candidate_tests.facets: Positive only: one Locator (synthetic) asserts normalized() == "synthetic::component(add)/scenario[happy]" (model/lib.rs:1022-1036). No negative-rejection facet (no foreign/empty adapter, no reformatting attempt). Boundary untouched: the value contains no "::", so verbatim pass-through of a separator-bearing opaque value is unproven; single adapter, so "owning adapter" is not exercised.

E2E positive on the identity-bearing surface: persisted DA-002/DA-003 per-target verdicts must start_with "rust-cargo::" (m3_acceptance.rs:414-418), including the SRC-ID-addressed fixture, so prefix omission and declared-spelling substitution are both excluded on records. Prefix-only assertion, not full-string equality; no negative-rejection or reformatting facet.

Boundary/no-decomposition: 'rust-cargo::src/parser.rs::Parser::parse' (value itself containing "::") survives audit YAML write and re-read verbatim (records.rs:2614-2698). But the string is hand-authored, not produced by normalized(), so it binds persistence fidelity, not the identity construction. No positive-construction or rejection facet.
Guards a kind-precondition (a permanent SRC ID may not be a Source Target's canonical target, scan/lib.rs:1591-1606). Relevant to registry identity but silent on the Locator string form.
Uses a prefixed locator literal only as fixture input for per-target set-mismatch handling (verify/lib.rs:2411-2432). Asserts nothing about canonical string composition.
Synthetic targets round-trip as a structured `targets` JSON list (w1_acceptance_binding.rs:487-510); the normalized string form is never produced or asserted.

details.contradiction_evidence: None. The implementation is faithful: `TargetRef::normalized` is `format!("{adapter}::{value}")` (crates/vtest-model/src/lib.rs:286-291), and every record-bearing path uses it verbatim (exec/lib.rs:177, audit/lib.rs:244,325, cli/lib.rs:1632, verify/lib.rs:2257); live `.verify/audits/*.yaml` carry `rust-cargo::…`. Core also enforces the owning adapter (scan/lib.rs:276-292). The one prefix-dropping site, `target_string` in core (scan/operations.rs:693-699, `adapter.as_str() == RUST_ADAPTER_ID => value.clone()`), feeds only the `@vtest.target` annotation render (operations.rs:571) and its idempotency compare, and round-trips through the adapter's own `Locator::parse`/`as_target` (adapter-rust/discovery.rs:55-76) — the declaration syntax the spec assigns to the adapter (基本仕様 §3.3), not the canonical identity.
details.notes: Three facets unproven: (1) rejection of a Locator whose adapter is not the owning one — the check at scan/lib.rs:289-292 has no test; (2) no normalized() test with "::" inside the opaque value (decomposition risk untested at the construction site); (3) no end-to-end full-string equality, only prefix. Evidence composes over one surface (normalized() → records) but covers positive+boundary partially and rejection not at all → PARTIAL. Adjacent, not in scope: target_string is a core-holds-adapter-knowledge leak (REQ-ADAPTER-BOUNDARY) belonging to another VO; AF-048 (exec records a SrcId-addressed declared spelling) concerns a different reference kind and is already red, owed to W5.
